Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old active female with 2-week history of right > left knee pain and clicking while running; concerned about overuse injury.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Knee pain and audible clicking, mainly right knee, onset ~2 weeks ago after increasing running mileage for marathon training (now 7–8 mile runs).
- Course/character: Pain begins ~20 min into run; requires stopping; occasional swelling after first run resolved with ice; clicking felt during leg extension exercises; no current resting pain.
- Associated symptoms: One episode of right toe tingling post-run; no giving way, locking, instability, stair difficulty, or persistent swelling/redness; full flexion/extension maintained.
- Pertinent negatives: No back pain, other joint involvement, calf pain, color/temperature change, or systemic symptoms.
- Past medical history: Hyperopia corrected with LASIK; remote severe UTI/kidney stone evaluation; otherwise healthy.
- Medications: Ibuprofen 400 mg PRN; naproxen (Aleve) dose/route/frequency not documented; vitamin D; melatonin; Xanax PRN (dose not documented); occasional cannabis joint.
- Allergies: Not discussed (missing).
- Social: Trains for marathon; plays ice hockey; occasional cannabis use; no other social history provided.
- Preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- No in-person exam performed (video consultation).
- Vitals: Not recorded.

Impression:
- Likely overuse/right knee soft-tissue injury (possible patellofemoral pain or cartilage/ligament strain); further assessment required.

Plan:
- Continue ice therapy frequently.
- Reduce running intensity; stop activity if pain occurs.
- Prescribe stronger oral non-steroidal anti-inflammatory (specific agent/dose not documented) to be taken with food; avoid concurrent ibuprofen.
- Refer to physiotherapy for comprehensive knee examination and management programme.
- Consider in-clinic assessment and imaging if physiotherapy appointment delayed or if clinical findings warrant.
- Red flags: Seek urgent medical review for persistent or increasing swelling, heat, redness, fever, severe pain, or knee locking/inability to move.
- Follow-up: Await physiotherapy; return sooner if symptoms worsen or red-flag signs develop.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Allergies status, detailed medication doses/frequencies, objective physical exam, vitals.
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.
● Transcript clear; minor conversational noise but clinically adequate.
